answer.question: What matters most in a small Neptune Beach turf yard?
answer.answer: The edges, access and daily use are visible all at once. Choose how turf meets the patio and planting, and leave walking room to gates and services. A compact green or pet area should serve the space rather than compete for every corner.

blocks.kicker: A yard seen from the back door
blocks.h2: Make the outline work from the start.
paras: A cottage lot or a yard reduced by a larger rebuilt home may have little space to spare. Plan useful walking routes first, then compare a lawn, dog area or short putting line. Extra cups do not help if there is no comfortable place to stand.
Discuss seams and transitions to paving or beds with the layout. Ask for removal, preparation and finishing to be clear in the written estimate.

Under mature trees, resolve applicable root and drip-line requirements before preparation. Near the beach, include blown sand and debris in the cleaning discussion. For pets, allow for waste pickup, cleaning access and time out of full sun.

Neptune Beach is its own city, separate from Jacksonville and Jacksonville Beach. Confirm applicable lot-coverage and landscape requirements for the parcel, plus any association conditions, before finalizing the footprint.

blocks.h2: In a yard this size, you see every seam.
paras: Neptune Beach has 2.34 square miles of land, the least of any of the Jacksonville Beaches (Wikipedia). Its streets filled with 1930s to 1950s summer cottages, built by Jacksonville families as beach getaways, then ranch houses from the '50s to the '70s, all on small platted lots. When an old house comes down, the new one tends to fill more of the lot, and the yard shrinks again.

A small yard is seen all at once, from the back door and the kitchen window, so the finish is most of the job. We lay the turf, seam it and edge it against the fence and the patio, then add the infill, finish it and clean up. Before we leave, we walk you through the care it needs.
A small yard also takes every step. The dog runs the same line along the fence, the kids cut the same corner, and grass in a space this tight never gets a rest. Turf doesn't need one.

blocks.h2: Its own city, and usually no HOA.
paras: Neptune Beach became a city on 11 August 1931, when it split from Jacksonville Beach in a dispute over taxes, and it stayed out of the 1968 consolidation with Jacksonville (Wikipedia). So it keeps its own code and building department, even though residents also vote for Jacksonville's mayor.

The city is an old platted grid, not a covenant subdivision, so most homes answer to no HOA and no architectural committee. Before the layout is final, ask the city whether a lot-coverage limit applies to your lot, and keep the answer in writing.

blocks.h2: City wells, still on the district's one-day schedule.
paras: Neptune Beach runs its own water utility, separate from JEA and from Jacksonville Beach: three wells drawing from the Floridan Aquifer, with a treatment plant on Forest Avenue (City of Neptune Beach).

The St. Johns River Water Management District declared a Phase III extreme water shortage for Duval County in mid-May 2026. Under it you get one watering day a week, Saturday for odd addresses and Sunday for even, never between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., with no more than 3/4 inch and one hour per zone (SJRWMD watering restrictions). Watering in new sod and new plantings is limited as well.
Turf takes that part of the yard off the schedule for good: no zone to run on your one day, and no brown patch to wait out until the order lifts.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Neptune Beach, FL?
faq.a: We install artificial turf, pet turf and backyard putting greens in Neptune Beach, FL. The lots here are small and old, so the finish shows from the back door. The city runs its own water system from its own wells, and it still falls under the St. Johns River Water Management District's 2026 order limiting lawns to one watering day a week. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: Can the city ban artificial turf?
faq.a: Not on a single-family lot of an acre or less, if the turf meets the state standard (Fla. Stat. 125.572). That standard allows natural infill such as clean sand, and rubber only under play equipment (DEP Rule 62-308.100). Our Florida infill guide has the rest.

faq.q: I'm on city water. Do the district's watering limits apply to me?
faq.a: Yes. The Phase III order covers every source in Duval County, city systems and private wells and pumps alike (St. Johns River Water Management District). Your utility is the city's own, but your watering day is set by the district.

faq.q: Can an HOA stop me putting in turf?
faq.a: Most Neptune Beach homes have no HOA to ask. Where there is one, Florida law bars it from restricting artificial turf that can't be seen from the frontage, a neighbor's lot, a common area or a community golf course (Fla. Stat. 720.3045). Turf the street can see is a different matter, so put that part of the plan to the board in writing.

faq.q: Is there room for a putting green in a Neptune Beach yard?
faq.a: Usually, if it's compact: two or three cups and a fringe fit most back yards here. There's no course inside the city. Atlantic Beach Country Club sits just north on Selva Marina Drive, and Jacksonville Beach Golf Club, run by that city, sits just south.
